name: De tai chanh
summary: Dê tái chanh is rare mountain goat dressed with lime, eaten wrapped in sung leaf and dipped in soy sauce. The meat is firm, because the goats climb the limestone. The tourism center’s Tam Coc day, updated 14 May 2025, names dê tái chanh with cơm cháy and dê nướng as the 11:45 lunch at a local restaurant after Tam Coc, Bích Động, and Thái Vi, and names no restaurant and no street. A 13 November 2020 provincial goat note describes thin slices with a thick lean part and the skin, passed through boiling water, then mixed with nước cốt chanh, gừng, tỏi, ớt, tiêu, and shredded lá chanh, and does not mention Tam Coc. The 20 October 2023 culture office still places tái dê in the city or the old capital.
origin: Ninh Bình. The culture page names it among the dê núi dishes on the roads toward the sights.
howToEat: Eat it with sung leaves, dipped in soy sauce, as Sở Văn hóa và Thể thao instructs.

The 13 November 2020 provincial note says kẹp chuối xanh, sả, and sung quả, and chấm tương bần. That note does not mention Tam Coc. The 14 May 2025 Tam Coc day prints the name and no method. The city method, with toasted sesame, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaf, ginger, and tương gừng, stays with the city or the old capital and is not the same kitchen.
where: The roads and lanes toward Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính.

A local restaurant on the 14 May 2025 Tam Coc day, after Tam Coc, Bích Động, and Thái Vi. No hamlet and no street. The printed lunch time is 11:45. A standing hour for a walk-up table is Check on arrival.
seoTitle: De tai chanh — Ninh Binh goat
seoDescription: Dê tái chanh in Ninh Bình, eaten with sung leaves and soy sauce, on the roads toward the karst sights.
